0.original: Sisipu would have you learn a new technique.

1.original: Using the technique the acting guildmaster has termed “fishwheeling” (more widely known as mooching), you are to use a crayfish ball to catch a striped goby, and then recast the goby in order to catch a shadow catfish. The fish can be found in the waters surrounding Fallgourd Float in the North Shroud.

2.original: Sisipu expresses her gratitude for the shadow catfish and seems genuinely impressed by how far you have come in the field of fishing.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※The next fisher quest will be available from Sisipu upon reaching level 30.

24.original: Deliver a shadow catfish to Sisipu.

48.original: You're familiar with the Culinarians' Guild, aren't you, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>? If you couldn't tell by its supercilious name, their members are a finicky bunch, particularly the fussy Master Lyngsath.

49.original: So when he comes asking for shadow catfish, no other fish will do, even if I kindly explain that fishing one out involves an arduous journey to Fallgourd Float followed by grueling labor. Naturally, I thought of you for the task.

50.original: This will likely require a bit of “fishwheeling,” if you know what I mean, though I imagine you do not, as I just invented that word. It means recasting a fish you've just caught as bait for a yet larger fish.

51.original: In my wisdom, I have deemed that your fishing prowess, land-faring acumen, and physical presence directly in front of me qualify you as the ideal candidate for the job.

52.original: I have no doubts you'll be more than amply capable of fishwheeling or any other new terms I see fit to conjure up, for that matter.

53.original: Simply use crayfish balls to catch a striped goby, then recast that to catch the shadow catfish.

54.original: Take it from the inventor of fishwheeling: since the striped goby will become your lure, you'll want to catch the biggest, shiniest one you can find.

55.original: A long journey lies ahead of you, and I fear the guild will not be the same in your absence. However, I choose to think of it not as losing a friend, but gaining a shadow catfish. Good luck!

56.original: Fishwheeling, or <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>mooching<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> as it is more widely known, involves catching a large fish and then recasting your line with the fish still on it in an attempt to land even larger prey. A high <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>perception<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> rating will increase your chances of catching fish of large size.

57.original: You'll find the catfish you seek at Fallgourd Float in the North Shroud. Mayhap it's a tad presumptuous to say you <hex:021A020203>will<hex:021A020103> find one, but that's where they are, at any rate.

58.original: Lyngsath ought to crack a smile when he glimpses this beauty.

59.original: They say never to look a gift fish in the mouth, but one can't help but stare at that gaping grimace─it looks like it could swallow a person whole!

60.original: I'm sure the fish of Gridania are none too displeased to see this one leave the water.

61.original: I heard that yarzons covet the fish too, sometimes migrating north and attacking fishermen in hopes of stealing the catch. Suppose I should've warned you about that ahead of time.

62.original: Still, I don't see what all the fuss is about. For all the lengths one need travel and dangers one need brave, the fish tastes little better than mud...

63.original: Pssst! Pardon me, but perhaps I might persuade you to prepare them in a proper bath? Water washes off the waste you can wipe away, but the invisible vapors only vanish with vinegar! You must mind the mud you can't see.

64.original: Speaking of the mud you can't see, where did you come out of all of a sudden!?

65.original: A good guildmaster gusts in and goes out a gale. Now you see me, now you don't!

66.original: Actually, I think we both still see you standing right there.

67.original: But that is neither here nor there. <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>─there are few fishermen who could haul in the catch you did today.

68.original: Frankly, I've started to wonder how we ever got along without you!
